summary: No blocking security findings were identified in the foundation scope. Secret-bearing settings are loaded from environment/.env, redacted diagnostics are available, generated/local sensitive files are ignored, SQLite uses technical-state tables only, and technical error routing is isolated to the error bot boundary.

checks.name: Secret handling
checks.evidence: No literal production secrets are present; .env and credential-like files are ignored; config redaction redacts token/credential keyed settings.

checks.name: Notification routing
checks.evidence: TECHNICAL_ERROR ignores supplied user/report recipients and sends only to admin_error_recipient through error_bot.

checks.name: SQLite boundary
checks.evidence: Schema creates technical-state tables and tests assert business-primary tables are not created.

checks.name: Path traversal and public URL avoidance
checks.evidence: Path fragments reject absolute paths, traversal, nested path fragments, and URL-like strings; default paths are local.

residualRisks.description: StoragePathPolicy root directories are configurable dataclass fields and are not validated as local-only roots. Defaults are safe and current tests cover default outputs, but future code that accepts root values from user-controlled input should validate roots too.
residualRisks.recommendation: When root paths become configurable from settings, validate them with a root-specific local-path guard before use.

residualRisks.description: redact_value only redacts strings containing token/secret/password/credential/api_key. Current Settings.as_dict redaction is protected by secret-like keys, but arbitrary standalone secret values without these substrings would not be redacted.
residualRisks.recommendation: Keep using redact_mapping for settings/log records; if arbitrary values are logged later, prefer key-aware redaction or explicit sensitive-field metadata.
